title: Real-time Chat Messaging Application
question: Design a real-time messaging system like WhatsApp or Slack. How do you handle 1-on-1 and group chats, message delivery status, and offline storage?

rubric.name: requirements_functional
rubric.description: Clarifies 1-on-1 vs group chat scale, media attachments, online presence, and message receipt status (sent/delivered/read).

rubric.name: realtime_connection_architecture
rubric.description: Uses WebSockets / long polling managed by a dedicated WebSocket Gateway cluster with service registry.

rubric.name: message_storage_data_model
rubric.description: Selects write-heavy NoSQL database (e.g. Cassandra or HBase) partitioned by `channel_id` / `chat_id` and ordered by `message_id` (Snowflake).

rubric.name: push_offline_delivery
rubric.description: Handles offline users via push notifications and syncs unread messages upon client reconnection.

rubric.name: scalability_tradeoffs
rubric.description: Addresses group chat fan-out issues, presence heartbeats, and message sequencing.

expected_signals: Chooses WebSockets for bi-directional persistent connections
Uses distributed ID generator (e.g. Snowflake) for monotonic message ordering
Distinguishes online WebSocket delivery from offline push notification fallback
red_flags: Uses client HTTP polling every second for real-time messaging
Relies on auto-increment SQL primary key for distributed multi-datacenter ordering
Ignores fan-out challenge for large group chats
follow_up_prompts: How would you generate globally unique, chronological message IDs across multiple chat servers?
How do you track user online status efficiently without overloading the database with heartbeats?
